subject: Request for documents - general rate application
body:
Good afternoon,

I hope this message finds you well, and thank you in advance for taking the time to read what has turned into a rather long note. I work for a small consumer advocacy group in Dartmouth, and over the past several months we have been trying to follow the various proceedings before the Nova Scotia Utility and Review Board that affect residential electricity customers. Some of our volunteers attended the public sessions in person, and others followed along from home, but we have found it surprisingly difficult to keep track of what was filed when, and which documents actually set out the Board's reasoning as opposed to the many procedural letters that accompany a proceeding of this size.

Last year we looked closely at another proceeding, but that work is finished and we have everything we need from it. This year our focus is squarely on the general rate application, and in particular on how the Board weighed the arguments about fuel costs, the deferral account, and the proposed phase-in for low-income customers. Our board of directors meets next month, and I have been asked to prepare a short briefing note that summarizes the key decisions and the principal filings so that our members can understand what was decided and why. I would much rather point them to the original documents than to newspaper coverage, which has been uneven at best.

With that in mind, would you be able to send me the key documents for matter M12205? I understand those include the application itself and the Board's decisions and orders, which is exactly what I need. I do not need the exhibits or the hearing recordings at this stage; our volunteers have already reviewed most of the evidence, and the recordings would be far too large for our purposes. If there is a limit on how many documents you can send at once, the most recent ones would be the most useful to us.

Thank you again for providing this service. It is genuinely helpful for small organizations like ours that do not have the resources to monitor regulatory proceedings full time. Please do not hesitate to let me know if you need any further information from me.

With warm regards,

Margaret Doucette
Volunteer Coordinator

subject: Thesis research - interrogatory responses
body:
Hello there,

My name is Daniel and I'm a graduate student at the University of Waterloo writing a thesis on how the Ontario Energy Board uses the interrogatory process to test utility evidence in rebasing applications. My supervisor suggested that I look at a recent large proceeding as a case study, and after some reading I have settled on the Enbridge Gas rebasing case, EB-2024-0111, because it has an unusually rich written record and the questions asked by intervenors span everything from capital planning to energy transition risk.

I have already downloaded the application and the pre-filed evidence from the Board's website, and I have read the procedural orders that set out the schedule, so I have a reasonable sense of how the case unfolded. What I am missing is a convenient way to look at the responses the applicant gave to the written questions. The RDS search interface is powerful, but it is not easy to use when you are trying to pull a specific set of records and I keep ending up with hundreds of results that I then have to sort through by hand, which takes hours. I also tried the advanced search with the case number and a document type filter, but the filter labels don't match the terms used in the procedural orders, so I was never quite sure whether I had everything or had accidentally excluded half of what I was looking for.

For my purposes I don't need everything. Could you please send me the three most recent interrogatory responses in that proceeding? Three should be enough for me to build out the coding scheme I'm developing, and if it works well I may come back and ask for more. I am not interested in the cost claims or the correspondence, only the interrogatory material.

I really appreciate any help you can offer. Tools like this make public records far more accessible to researchers, and I'd be glad to acknowledge the service in my thesis if that would be welcome. Thank you so much for your time, and I hope you have a pleasant rest of the week.

Best wishes,
Daniel Okafor
MASc Candidate, Department of Systems Design Engineering

subject: Comments in the interconnection rulemaking
body:
Hi,

I'm a policy analyst at a regional clean energy nonprofit, and I've been asked to put together a brief for our members on how stakeholders responded to the Commission's interconnection reforms. As you probably know, the rulemaking that produced Order No. 2023 drew an enormous volume of public input from transmission providers, developers, state commissions, and public interest organizations, and I'd like to characterize the main themes of that input accurately rather than relying on secondhand summaries from trade press, which tend to emphasize whichever parties were most quotable rather than most representative.

Our members are particularly interested in what was said about the cluster study process, the readiness deposits, and the penalties for delayed studies, because several of them have projects sitting in queues right now and the practical implications are significant for their financing. A few of them have also asked whether the positions taken by the larger transmission providers were broadly shared or whether they stood apart from the rest of the record, which is the kind of question I can only answer from the filings. I've already read the final order and the rehearing order, and I'm comfortable with the legal outcome; what I want now is to understand the positions that commenters took before the Commission made its decision, and how those positions shifted between the initial and reply rounds.

So my request is fairly simple: could you send me the comments filed in RM22-14? The most recent ones are fine if there's a cap on how many you can send in one go. I don't need the orders themselves or the notices, since I already have those on file from when they were issued.

Thanks very much for your help with this. I've found the service genuinely useful in the past, and it saves me a great deal of time compared with navigating eLibrary directly, which can be slow and difficult to search when you are looking for a particular class of filing in a docket with thousands of entries.

All the best,
Jordan Reyes
Policy Analyst

subject: Scheduling question
body:
Dear team,

I'm writing on behalf of a municipal electric utility that is following the Ontario Energy Board's proceeding EB-2025-0064 with some interest. We are not an intervenor and do not intend to become one, but the outcome may influence how we approach our own filing next year, and our council has asked staff to keep a close eye on the schedule so that we can brief them at the right moments.
